messages:
ravi.security: quick follow-up after the AuthN/AuthZ RFC review. want to lock down service-account semantics before the RFC PR. main goals: reduce blast radius, make scoping explicit, and keep runtime checks fast.

jen.pm: agreed. main question from PM: will this break existing API key usage for customers? need a migration story.

ravi.security: migration sketch: introduce two classes: human-api-key (SSO-backed, optional short TTL) and service-cred (minted by control plane, prefer certs). keep legacy keys as "legacy-compat" label for 12 months default, allow orgs to opt-in to rotate immediately. provide /keys/rotate endpoint that atomically issues new scoped cred and revokes old.

max.infra: storage note: only store keyed HMAC + metadata. never persist raw secret after mint. metadata fields we need: key_id, kind, org_id, project_id, roles, created_by, created_at, expires_at, rotation_policy. revocations in a compact revocation table + memcached bloom filter for quick checks.

iris.secalert: add: key_id should be UUID v4 prefixed with kind char (h- or s-), helps ops. also include key fingerprint in audit events.

ravi.security: good idea on prefixes. for scoping: support exact org/project pairs and also explicit cross-org delegation via signed grants. avoid star-scopes unless org admin enables.

sarah.dev: runtime evaluation: embedding full authz checks in hot path is costly. proposal: tokens carry compact claims (sub, key_id, roles[], scope_hash) and nodes validate claim signature + consult a local policy blob cache. policy blobs versioned; runtime rejects tokens issued against newer policy than it knows about? that could break.

ravi.security: don't reject; allow until token TTL. policy version included in token so audits know which policy applied. if an admin revokes, publish revocation event on pubsub to invalidate caches and add to revocation bloom.

max.infra: cert-based service auth: control-plane CA issues short-lived mTLS certs (1h) to workloads. identity = service://org/<org>/proj/<proj>/svc/<svc>. certs minted via a signed CSR flow over the control channel, with attestation from node agent. rotate CA key yearly; provide cross-signed intermediate for graceful rotation.

jen.pm: how do services call each other across org boundaries? we see usage for shared infra (billing, auth).

ravi.security: prefer delegation flow: service A requests a delegated token for service B with a narrowed set of scopes. delegation requires either preauthorized role or an explicit allowlist. delegation grants are signed, short-lived (5m), and auditable. avoids multi-scope long-lived tokens.

iris.secalert: impersonation/act-as: require an approver or a 2FA flag for humans. all impersonation events must include reason and be reversible. tokens get "impersonator" claim and TTL <= 15m.

sarah.dev: introspection endpoint: add a low-volume token introspect endpoint for admin tools and for rare runtime validation. not on hot path. runtime nodes should default to local validation + cache.

max.infra: cache invalidation: policy blobs have monotonic version; publish version bumps on pubsub. nodes subscribe and fetch new blob when bump arrives. use consistent hashing to shard cache refresh load.

jen.pm: enterprise SSO: support enforced SSO-only issuance for human keys, SCIM provisioning to sync org membership, and configurable retention for audit logs per org SLA.

ravi.security: audit schema: event_type, timestamp, key_id, key_kind, actor, resolved_roles, policy_version, decision, resource, action, attrs, request_id, src_ip (kept only for short retention by default). emit JSON lines to kafka and provide forwarder for enterprise SIEM.

iris.secalert: GDPR flag: mark personal data fields and rotate/erase after retention window. avoid storing raw IPs beyond 90 days by default.

sarah.dev: edge-case: batch jobs that need broad read-only access. suggestion: support "job" service accounts with constrained operations and time-bounded leases. lease manager auto-rotates creds on expiry.

ravi.security: yes. will include job accounts. also: admin UI for orgs to view active tokens, last-used, and rotate/revoke. UI actions emit audit events.

max.infra: telemetry: track token mint rate, revocation rate, cache hit ratio, avg policy blob propagation latency. set SLIs for revocation propagation.

jen.pm: next steps: ravi to write RFC addendum covering data model, mint/rotate endpoints, delegation flow, mTLS details, cache/invalidation design, audit schema, and migration plan. ask infra for scaling numbers.

token-bot: Reminder: follow-up RFC due 2025-02-11 assigned to ravi.security :calendar:
